milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Corrective

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Makes MCP approval evidence monotonic and latest-state based so a historical approved event cannot authorize execution after consumed, executing, stale, malformed, or outcome-unknown evidence.
Provides a public Runtime-owned mcp.tool.approve boundary and replay-safe execution claim semantics for autonomous controllers without granting CLI, VSIX, or model output approval authority.

Tightens the previously closed MCP-S4 approval binding baseline with atomic pre-spawn claim, terminal consumption, outcome-unknown handling, concurrent duplicate denial, and fail-closed key_required behavior until key validation exists.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement, headless_autonomous_development, and controlled_workspace_tools by turning MCP approval evidence into a Runtime-owned monotonic state machine.
answers.new_capability: Callers can use mcp.tool.approve to request a Runtime-computed approval binding, and approval-required MCP tools execute only after an atomic approved-to-executing claim immediately before tools/call.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S4 bound approvals to scoped fingerprints, but historical approved evidence could still be reused after later consumed evidence unless Runtime considered the latest approval state and claimed it atomically.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Approval-required MCP mutation tools could be retried or reused from stale durable approval evidence, leaving MCP execution unsafe despite S4 approval binding.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Runtime execution semantics and tests the previously missing consumed-state and concurrent-claim cases; it is not another approval-binding documentation pass.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. The phase intentionally adds mcp.tool.approve because previous tests relied on direct Store-written approval evidence, which is not a public Runtime boundary.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase does not add a diagnostic, report, digest, verdict, history, preview, or summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Approval-required MCP tools now require the latest matching state to be approved, claim that approval as executing under a run-local lock, terminalize it as consumed or outcome_unknown, deny duplicate/concurrent reuse, and fail closed for key_required idempotency until Runtime key validation exists.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers can approve one exact MCP invocation through Runtime and know that duplicate retries, stale approvals, and ambiguous outcome windows will not launch a second tools/call.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the MCP-S4.1 corrective debt while Runtime Release Ready remains false until the other recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers and owner license/publish decision are resolved.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S4.1 changes the Runtime release-readiness guard, boundary contract, audit, and current phase manifest. Review must confirm mcp.tool.approve is a Runtime-owned approval boundary, approval evidence is latest-state and consumption-safe, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: Runtime exposes mcp.tool.approve as a typed JSON-RPC method that recomputes approval binding evidence from task policy, live catalog, pinned catalog provenance, annotations, schema fingerprints, server identity, and structured MCP safety policy.

Approval-required MCP execution uses only the latest matching McpToolExecutionApproved state; historical approved evidence cannot beat later consumed, executing, outcome_unknown, stale, malformed, or terminal approval evidence.
Approved evidence is atomically claimed as executing immediately before tools/call under a run-local claim lock.
Successful, tool-error, schema-failed, or unsupported-input-required outcomes terminalize claimed approval as consumed; timeout or protocol-failure windows terminalize it as outcome_unknown.
Concurrent execution attempts for the same approval launch at most one tools/call.
idempotency=key_required fails closed until Runtime-owned concrete key pointer validation exists.
Runtime Release Readiness and MCP safety audits record MCP-S4.1 as corrective closure while Runtime Release Ready remains false.

brownie-runtime mcp_tool_public_approval_round_trip_executes_once_and_consumes_approval covers the public mcp.tool.approve boundary and one-shot consumption.
brownie-runtime mcp_tool_concurrent_same_approval_execution_launches_once covers the atomic execution claim.
brownie-runtime mcp_tool_timeout_after_approval_records_outcome_unknown_and_blocks_reuse covers ambiguous outcome fail-closed retry behavior.
Runtime release-readiness guard requires mcp.tool.approve in the canonical Runtime boundary method subset.

accepted_capability: MCP approval-required execution is latest-state, consumption-safe, and duplicate-retry safe.
mcp.tool.approve provides a public Runtime-owned approval boundary instead of relying on direct Store-written evidence.
MCP-S4.1 is closed as a corrective to the MCP Runtime Safety Policy baseline.
behavior_evidence: Runtime tests validate public approval, consumed-state denial, concurrent duplicate denial, timeout outcome_unknown denial, and key_required fail-closed behavior.
Runtime Release Readiness guard validates the canonical boundary includes mcp.tool.approve.
MCP and Runtime release audits document the corrected approval consumption and retry semantics.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the approval admission, claim, replay, ledger, permission, tool execution, and terminal evidence authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection/validation layers.

MCP approval evidence is narrowing-only and cannot grant completion, verification, permission, workspace mutation, Mode Pack policy, MCP access, catalog authority, schema authority, executable identity, or external-loop scheduling authority.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, registry, automatic install, hosted secret manager, remote Git expansion, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, hosted platform, forge/notification adapters, custom tool adapter protocols, package installation, signing infrastructure, or remote binary distribution.
Does not reopen MCP-S1 through MCP-S7 except for the targeted MCP-S4.1 approval-consumption corrective.
Does not close process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema migration, CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, or platform/deadline/durability blockers.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected scanning for any matching approved event because it permits historical approval reuse after consumed evidence.
Rejected direct Store-written approval as the acceptance boundary because callers need a Runtime-owned approval command.
Rejected metadata-only retry policy because Runtime must derive retry admissibility from durable approval attempt state.
Rejected key_required approval until Runtime has a concrete key pointer validation contract.
technical_debt: Remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers: real process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema version and migration, runtime-release-guard CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, runtime module decomposition reevaluation, and platform/deadline/durability hardening.
Owner license/publish decision remains required before OSS release basis can be claimed.
